title: Cinema
summary: Moving pictures began as a peepshow: Edison's Kinetoscope of 1894 showed one viewer at a time a 17-second scene. Projection to paying audiences came in 1895, first from the Lambda company's Eidoloscope in New York on 20 May, then the Skladanowsky brothers in Berlin in November. On 28 December 1895 Auguste and Louis Lumiere's Cinematographe, a compact camera and projector, showed ten films to 33 paying spectators at the Grand Cafe in Paris, and Lumiere operators soon set off to film around the world.

uncertainty.note: Exact date of the first commercial public screening at the Salon Indien du Grand Café in Paris.

as_recorded.value: 28 décembre 1895, au Grand Café à Paris

where.modern_name: Paris, France (site of the Grand Café on Boulevard des Capucines)

importance.justification: Created film, a mass medium that shaped twentieth-century culture worldwide (R4 D2 T3 L3).

related.because: BFI: the film business began with Edison's peepshow Kinetoscope of 1894.

beats.caption: The Lumière brothers present the first commercial screening of projected motion pictures at the Grand Café in Paris.
Projected film rapidly spreads internationally, inaugurating permanent movie theaters and a global cinematic mass entertainment industry.
